text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: Service `inference-frontend-prod` exceeded 5xx rate threshold (alert: inference-5xx-surge). PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PDR98765 — page fired to #incidents.

Sam Carter: acked the page — I'm oncall but currently on a support call. marking as `ack` and handing ownership to @Maya for initial triage. @Maya can you confirm? :point_down:

Maya Chen: taking it. I'm jumping in now. first glance: dashboards show a sudden 5xx spike starting ~2m ago, primarily EU region, and request latency also rising. Noted increased error rate against model 'redwood-3b-quant' route.

Priya Narayanan: tagging customer-impact — we have a support ticket (SUP-4521) indicating some customers reporting timeouts. Estimated affected TPS ~2.1% of global traffic but concentrated on EU.

Maya Chen: running quick checks — getting pod logs and deployment status.

Maya Chen: ```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-backend -o wide
kubectl -n prod logs deployment/inference-backend -c server --since=5m | grep ERROR | tail -40
```

Maya Chen: logs show repeated OOMKilled+crashloop on pod inference-backend-7f6d9 due to a memory spike during KV cache warmup after a model roll; also saw a surge of traffic routed to that pod by connection stickiness.

Jorge Ruiz: @Maya that pod was part of the new canary we rolled 6h ago. I pushed a config that increases `max_cache_mem` last night. Could be related.

Maya Chen: will scale down the canary and redistribute. Plan: 1) cordon and drain the problematic pod, 2) bump replicas to absorb traffic, 3) revert canary config if needed.

Ash Patel: if we drain, traffic should route to other healthy pods, but watch autoscaler — if it tries to scale up more canaries we might reintroduce the bad config. Suggest temporarily pause rollout.

Maya Chen: executing now.

Maya Chen: ```
kubectl -n prod cordon inference-backend-7f6d9
kubectl -n prod drain inference-backend-7f6d9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/inference-backend --replicas=12
kubectl -n prod annotate deployment/inference-backend rollout-paused=true --overwrite
```

pagerbot: Note: autoscaler event at 2287658980 — scaling decision in-flight. Recommend manually reconciling after scale.

Maya Chen: after drain, starting to see 5xx rate drop — currently down from 8.4% to 1.9% globally, EU down to 1.5%. Still watching.

Sam Carter: thanks @Maya. I'm oncall to assist if anything else pops. switching to watch mode.

Priya Narayanan: customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased error rates for inference requests in EU. Short-term mitigation in progress. We'll post updates every 15 minutes." Do we want to send now?

Maya Chen: hold for one more status update — looks like mitigation working, but want to ensure stable for 5m.

Jorge Ruiz: I'm looking at the canary config diff now. The `max_cache_mem` change increases resident set and apparently led to transient OOM when multiple requests hit simultaneously. That explains crashloop.

Maya Chen: temp mitigation: revert canary config and roll it back.

Maya Chen: ```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/inference-backend -c server MAX_CACHE_MEM=1G
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/inference-backend
kubectl -n prod annotate deployment/inference-backend rollout-paused=false --overwrite
```

Maya Chen: rollback triggered, rolling pods to stable config. 5xx rate down to 0.4% now. EU region showing near-normal traffic.

oncall-sre: escalating note — please file follow-up to ensure autoscaler and rollout pipeline blocks on canary health checks; we don't want an automated rollout reintroducing this.

Ash Patel: filed ticket OPS-1258 to add guardrails on canary memory knob and add pod-level OOM alert. Assigned to eng-runtime.

Priya Narayanan: sending customer update now: "Mitigation in place; traffic returned to normal levels. We'll follow up with a root-cause update once investigation completes." Sent to affected customers via support tool (SUP-4521 updated).

Sam Carter: good work. status: mitigation stable, incident can be transitioned to 'monitoring'. Leaving ownership with @Maya for postmortem.

Maya Chen: will own the follow-up. Immediate next steps: 1) capture logs from crashloop pod (inference-backend-7f6d9), 2) run `heaptrack` style sampling in staging to reproduce, 3) update rollout pipeline to block canary until steady for 30m.

Maya Chen: saved logs and attached to incident PDR98765. ```
kubectl -n prod logs inference-backend-7f6d9 -c server --previous > /tmp/oom-7f6d9.log
```

Jorge Ruiz: also adding a temporary traffic-shaping rule to avoid sticky routing to single pod during rollout windows.

pagerbot: Incident PDR98765 status changed: acknowledged -> monitoring. Responders: Maya Chen (owner), Sam Carter (oncall), Jorge Ruiz (runtime). Duration: ~18 minutes from page to monitoring.

Maya Chen: closing the realtime paging thread. I'll post a short follow-up summary and schedule a 30m postmortem with eng-runtime and SRE to decide permanent fixes.

Priya Narayanan: tagging for customer-facing RCA: @Sam @Maya please coordinate a succinct explanation (root cause: mis-tuned canary memory param causing OOM under warmup traffic; mitigation: rollback + drain + autoscale reconciliation). ETA for RCA draft: EOD today.

Sam Carter: acknowledged. If anything resurfaces ping me directly `@Sam`.

Maya Chen: final note — no additional customer-facing incidents reported after mitigation. Leaving channel in 10m. :white_check_mark:
